_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

personal_token.label: API key
personal_token.where: Granola desktop app > Settings > Connectors > API keys > Create new key. Tick the note access scopes on the creation screen.
notes: A personal key needs a Business plan. On Enterprise an admin can restrict which scopes members may use in Settings > Workspace > General > API access for members - so a scope missing from the creation screen is workspace policy, not a bug.
A personal key is tied to its owner's account and expires. A workspace key does not; prefer that one for anything scheduled.
Scopes on a personal key can be edited after the fact (Settings > Connectors > API keys > Edit), unlike most vendors. Revoking is still permanent and cannot be undone.
There is no sandbox. Test against a small dedicated folder.

workspace_key.label: Workspace API key
workspace_key.where: Granola desktop app > Settings > Connectors > Workspace API keys. Admins only.
notes: Belongs to the workspace rather than a person, does not expire, and keeps working after the admin who made it leaves. The better choice for a workflow that has to keep running.

Reaches public notes, plus any space with 'Allow Granola API access' turned on - which is ON by default for a newly created space, including its folders and subfolders. Worth saying out loud to anyone enabling this.
Cannot read private notes or unshared folders at all.
If the workspace has 'Allow public folders' turned off, public notes are not exposed to the API even with this key.

scopes.personal_notes: Notes the key owner owns, notes shared directly with them, and notes in private folders shared with them.
scopes.public_notes: Notes visible to everyone in the workspace, including the Team space.
scopes.note: Notes are private by default. A note only appears under public_notes if it sits in a folder visible to the whole workspace. Both scopes can be on one key. An empty result is almost always a scope or folder-visibility question rather than an API fault.

pagination.response: hasMore (boolean) and cursor - note the camelCase, which the rest of the payload does not use

api.ids: Note IDs are prefixed not_ and are not UUIDs. A UUID seen elsewhere in Granola is a different identifier and will not resolve here.
api.visibility: The API only returns notes that have BOTH a generated AI summary and a transcript. A note still processing, or never summarised, is silently absent from the list and 404s on a direct get - so an empty result is usually processing state or scope, not a fault.

list_notes.notes: Returns { notes, hasMore, cursor }. The natural shape for an incremental sync: keep the last created_after and page until hasMore is false.

get_note.notes: Carries title, owner, summary and, with include=transcript, the transcript inline. Returns 413 with error code TRANSCRIPT_TOO_LARGE when the transcript will not fit - fall back to the transcript endpoint rather than retrying.

get_transcript.notes: The complete transcript, and the required fallback for a 413 from get_note.

rate_limits.note: Scoped per user or per workspace depending on the key, so several workflows sharing a workspace key share one bucket.

webhooks.note: Flux has no public endpoint to register, so it polls list_notes. Recorded in full because the signature scheme is the part people get wrong.
webhooks.registration: Body is { url, scopes, folder_ids? }. The URL must be HTTPS and publicly reachable - private-network addresses are rejected. scopes are personal and/or public, the same two that gate API keys. Omitting events subscribes to all of them. folder_ids narrows to those folders and their subfolders, and the scopes must match the folder's visibility.

events.note.generated: The first AI summary for a note is generated.
events.note.edited: The summary is edited or regenerated. Carries data.changed_fields, currently always ['summary'].
events.note.access_granted: A note is shared with you, directly or via a folder.
events._: note.generated only fires if the endpoint could already see the note. A note generated earlier and shared later arrives as note.access_granted instead - subscribe to both or discovery has a hole.

webhooks.payload: { event_id, event_type, note_id, occurred_at }. No note content: fetch it with the API key, and access is checked at fetch time, so a delivery can never leak more than the API would.

signature.spec: Standard Webhooks (standardwebhooks.com) - any conforming library verifies it.
signature.headers: webhook-id (equals event_id), webhook-timestamp (unix seconds), webhook-signature ('v1,' then base64 HMAC-SHA256).
signature.key: The signing secret with the whsec_ prefix stripped, then base64-decoded. Using the raw string as the key is the usual bug.
rules: Verify over the raw body and parse the JSON only afterwards.
webhook-signature can hold several space-separated versioned signatures; accept if any v1 entry matches, and compare in constant time.
Reject a webhook-timestamp more than a few minutes old, or the signature does not stop a replay.
signature.secret: signing_secret is returned only in the create response and never again - not in list. Losing it means recreating the endpoint.

delivery.retried: 408, 429, 5xx, network errors and timeouts - exponential backoff for four days, reusing event_id so deliveries can be deduplicated.
delivery.permanent_failure: 3xx (redirects are not followed) and any other 4xx.
delivery.disabled: After four days with no success Granola disables the endpoint and emails its creator or the workspace admins. Events missed while disabled are NOT replayed - after re-enabling, backfill through list_notes with created_after.

also_ships.mcp: Granola publishes an MCP server that uses browser-based OAuth and is aimed at conversational assistants rather than scripts. Not what this connector uses - an API key is the right shape for a scheduled workflow - but it is the path if a skill ever wants OAuth instead of a pasted key.

notes: The base URL, the grn_ key prefix, the three endpoints, the cursor shape, the not_ ID form, the 413 TRANSCRIPT_TOO_LARGE fallback, the transcript speaker shapes and the rate limits are taken verbatim from Granola's own API reference.
docs.granola.ai is not reachable from the Flux container - the egress proxy refuses the CONNECT - so this was written from the pages the user supplied rather than fetched.
The webhook guide has now been read; its event list, signature construction and retry policy are recorded verbatim.

transcript_shape.note: Transcript items differ by the platform that recorded them, which matters to anything attributing lines to people.
transcript_shape.macos: speaker.source is 'microphone' (the local mic) or 'speaker' (other meeting audio). Two streams, so who-said-what is separable at the local/remote level but not per remote person.
transcript_shape.ios: speaker.source is currently always 'microphone' because the app captures a single stream, with an optional diarization_label carrying an anonymous 'Speaker A/B/...' bucket. Do not treat source as a reliable discriminator - Granola says explicitly that clients should not assume this stays single-stream.

pending_operations.note: The webhook-endpoint CRUD above is documented but not exposed as a Flux operation, since Flux cannot host a receiver. List folders (referenced by the webhook guide as /api-reference/list-folders) has not been read and is the one remaining read worth having - it is how a folder-scoped sync would work.
